items.title: Google AI Mode Cites Itself More Often, With More Organic Links
items.summary: Google's self-referencing in AI Mode has tripled over nine months, now accounting for 17% of all citations, with a shift where 59% of these point to organic search results rather than Google Business Profiles. SE Ranking's analysis shows Google as the top-cited domain in 19 of 20 niches, indicating broader relevance beyond local search. This underscores the ongoing importance of traditional SEO for visibility in AI-generated responses.

items.title: GEO & AEO: How to Get Cited by AI Search in 2026
items.summary: AI engines like ChatGPT and Perplexity cite sources in synthesized answers, shifting from SEO to GEO/AEO for visibility without clicks. Tactics include citation triggers (up to 115% lift per Princeton research), checklists, templates, and tracking with Otterly.ai. Optimize structured content for authority and citations to combat zero-click searches.

items.title: Authors Guild Expands AI-Free Certification Program to Publishers and Non-Members
items.summary: The Authors Guild has broadened its Human Authored certification, launched in 2025, to include publishers and non-Guild members, enabling them to verify books as human-written with a trademarked seal. Over 3,000 authors have certified 5,000 titles, excluding minor AI aids like grammar checks. This responds to AI-generated content flooding the market and reader preferences for human-authored books.

items.title: Publishers Weekly Book Deals: Harlan Coben Memoir and Taylor Sheridan Survival Guide Acquired
items.summary: Grand Central acquired North American rights to Harlan Coben's 'Plot Twist: Life, Craft and the Messy First Draft,' a memoir on writing set for September release. Simon & Schuster secured 'How to Not Die in Prison' by Taylor Sheridan and Tom Nelson, a nonfiction survival guide for June publication. Other notable deals include thrillers like 'Eternal Glow' in a five-book series.

items.title: Scholastic Lands Six-Figure Deal for Libba Bray's YA Romance 'Radio Free Texas'
items.summary: Scholastic's David Levithan acquired North American rights in a six-figure deal to Libba Bray's 'Radio Free Texas,' a teen romance centered on an indie radio station, slated for fall 2026. Other children's deals include YA supernatural mysteries, cozy romances, and middle-grade fantasy series. These acquisitions highlight strong interest in YA genres popular on BookTok.

items.title: Vulture Analyzes Conservative-Coded Themes in New Books by Madeline Cash and Honor Levy
items.summary: Vulture reviews Madeline Cash's debut 'Lost Lambs' and Honor Levy's 'My First Book,' noting their ironic provocations against wokeness and progressive culture through traditional family sagas and edgy satire. Cash's novel features QAnon-inspired plots and redemption arcs in an all-white suburban setting. The works employ shock value and reactionary politics to defend white identity.

items.title: Literary Agents Update Guidelines to Ban AI-Generated Submissions
items.summary: Multiple literary agencies now reject manuscripts and cover letters created using generative AI, as reported by The Times. This policy aims to preserve human creativity amid rising AI content in queries. Writers face automatic disqualification for AI use in submissions.

items.title: Grand Central Acquires George Saunders' New Novel and Writing Nonfiction in Major Two-Book Deal
items.summary: Random House secured world rights to two books by acclaimed author George Saunders, including an untitled novel and nonfiction on writing akin to 'A Swim in a Pond in the Rain.' The deal underscores continued investment in literary heavyweights. Publication dates are forthcoming.

items.title: Scary Movie 6: Is It Impossible To Make Comedies Without Woke Culture?
items.summary: The trailer for Scary Movie 6 features a scene mocking woke culture by having a character correct their gender assumption during a stabbing, highlighting how comedies often target such elements for humor. Some viewers were able to enjoy the film as pure entertainment and overlook potential offenses, while others expressed upset over a racist joke and the pronoun-related mockery. The article questions whether this approach signals the end of iconic comedies in the current climate.

items.title: Timothée Chalamet Faces Backlash After Saying 'No One Cares About' Ballet and Opera
items.summary: Timothée Chalamet received criticism from opera singers and ballet dancers on social media for claiming that no one cares about ballet and opera anymore while advocating for movie theaters. Performers such as Isabelle Leonard expressed shock at his views, calling them ineloquent and narrow-minded, while others like Deepa Johnny and Victor Caixeta emphasized the enduring value and historical significance of these art forms. Chalamet acknowledged the potential misstep during the discussion, noting he 'lost 14 cents in viewership.'

items.title: 'SNL' faces backlash for Tourette's sketch mocking BAFTAs racial slur incident
items.summary: A Tourette's charity condemned SNL for a sketch that mocked the BAFTAs racial slur incident by having characters blame their controversies on Tourette's syndrome. The charity's CEO stated that mocking a disability is never acceptable and emphasized that Tourette's is a complex neurological condition, not a joke. The sketch, released online after being cut from the broadcast, received swift condemnation from viewers and has garnered nearly 1 million views on YouTube.

items.title: God Of War Fans Pray For Ugly Sonic Fix After TV Actor Responds
items.summary: Fans reacted negatively to the first promotional image of Ryan Hurst as Kratos in Amazon's God of War TV show, leading to widespread confusion and bemusement online. Hurst responded cryptically on Instagram, urging fans not to believe everything they see, which has prompted some to hope the image is a flawed representation akin to the initial CGI Sonic design that was later revised. This backlash has fans speculating on potential improvements to the final product.

items.title: Box Office: 'Hoppers' To Spring $88M Global Opening, 'The Bride!' $40M
items.summary: Pixar’s Hoppers is projected to open to $88M globally across 41 markets, marking the best start for a Pixar original since Coco and the highest-reviewed since then at 97% on Rotten Tomatoes. In North America, it is expected to gross $36M-$38M at 4,000 theaters, with $45M-$50M from offshore markets. Warner Bros.’ The Bride!, directed by Maggie Gyllenhaal, is anticipated to debut with $38M-$40M worldwide, including $16M-$18M domestic and $22M international.

items.title: No AI Plan, No Loan. Small Business Lenders Force Main Street To Face The Future
items.summary: Small business lenders are increasingly requiring applicants to demonstrate how they are addressing the disruptive impact of artificial intelligence on their operations, as AI tools could automate tasks in industries like professional services and real estate where many small firms operate. This shift in underwriting standards means bankers must assess long-term business survival amid AI advancements, with some rejecting loans if AI threatens the business model, while others seek plans for adaptation to maintain competitiveness. Failure to engage with AI discussions can signal risks like lack of oversight or obsolescence, influencing loan approvals and terms.

items.title: AI tools and training for small businesses
items.summary: Google announced free resources to help small businesses understand and use artificial intelligence, including a new AI Professional Certificate program to build practical skills for business owners and teams. AI tools are increasingly integrated into business platforms for marketing, customer service, operations, and data analysis, with the challenge being where to start and how to use them effectively. Small businesses can access free training to build foundational AI skills and a Google Business Profile resource hub with guides, tutorials, and tips to strengthen online visibility.

items.title: Smart AI Adoption: Lessons for Small Businesses
items.summary: Small businesses adopting AI should prioritize governance by setting up data protections and avoiding unsecured tools before deployment to safeguard customer information. Leaders emphasize upskilling employees to use AI effectively, encouraging exploration while ensuring outputs align with business needs and fostering critical thinking. Building a culture of AI adoption involves commitment through internal discussions and practical experimentation to integrate tools like Microsoft Copilot into daily operations.
